Rutherfordium: Albert Ghiorso. Rutherfordium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rf and atomic number 104.
Who is credited with discovering Ampère's force law?
Ampère's force law: André-Marie Ampère. In magnetostatics, Ampère's force law describes the force of attraction or repulsion between two current-carrying wires.
Who is credited with discovering Rhenium?
Rhenium: Walter Noddack. Rhenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Re and atomic number 75.
This tsetse-fly-borne parasitic infection, caused by a protozoan, disproportionately affects humans and cattle across Africa — what is it?
Atrocities in the Congo Free State

African trypanosomiasis is an insect-borne parasitic infection of humans and other animals caused by the protozoan species Trypanosoma brucei, which is transmitted by the bite of an infected tsetse fly.
This group of large, semiaquatic boas native to tropical South America includes the green species, among the largest snakes on Earth — name the group?
Anaconda are a group of large boas of the genus Eunectes.
Considered a visual art even though it leans on civil engineering, this discipline gives us cultural symbols that often outlast the civilizations that built them. What is it?
Architecture is the study and practice of designing structures, especially habitable ones.

Originating in Central Africa and classified as a hound by the American Kennel Club, this dog breed doesn't bark but instead makes an unusual yodel-like sound due to its uniquely shaped larynx — what's the breed?
Basenji is a breed of hunting dog created from stock that originated in Central Africa, including in the Republic of the Congo and other adjacent tropical African countries.
This small bird in the Old World flycatcher family breeds among rocky habitats from the British Isles to Morocco and east to central China — what species is it?
Black redstart (Phoenicurus ochruros) is a small passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family.

Forced to flee Italy in 1938 under the racial laws, this experimental physicist had earlier invented an improved coincidence circuit and traveled to Eritrea to show cosmic rays arrived more strongly from the West than the East — who was he?
Bruno Rossi (13 April 1905 - 21 November 1993) was an Italian-American experimental physicist.

Honored twice by the American Psychological Association — in 1956 for scientific contributions and 1972 for professional ones — this psychologist championed a person-centered approach to therapy — who is he?
Carl Rogers (January 8, 1902 - February 4, 1987) was an American psychologist who was one of the founders of humanistic psychology and was known especially for his person-centered psychotherapy.
This plant-cell organelle uses chlorophyll pigments to capture sunlight and convert it into chemical energy, ultimately producing sugar via the Calvin cycle — what is it?
Chloroplast (-plahst) is a type of organelle known as a plastid that conducts photosynthesis mostly in plant and algal cells.

Ranging across most of Europe and into the Palearctic as far as northwestern China, this medium-sized bird of prey sees its northernmost populations migrate as far as South Africa each winter — which raptor?
Common buzzard (Buteo buteo) is a medium-sized bird of prey with a large range.

Caused by prolonged exposure to glucocorticoids like cortisol, this collection of symptoms includes abdominal weight gain with thin limbs, a rounded red face, and weak, fragile skin that heals poorly — what's it called?
Cushing's syndrome is a collection of signs and symptoms due to prolonged exposure to glucocorticoids such as cortisol.

This gut ailment flares up when small pouches in the wall of the large intestine become inflamed, often striking with sudden lower-abdominal pain — fever or bloody stool warns of a complication; what is it?
Diverticulitis is a gastrointestinal disease characterized by inflammation of abnormal pouches - diverticula - that can develop in the wall of the large intestine.
Many of these Northern Hemisphere shade trees, prized along old European and American streets, were wiped out by a fungus carried by bark beetles — which tree genus is this?
Elm are deciduous and semi-deciduous trees comprising the genus Ulmus in the family Ulmaceae.
First confirmed around a pulsar in 1992, this astronomical term describes any planet located outside our own solar system — over 6,300 have now been confirmed — what is it called?
Exoplanet is a planet outside the Solar System. The first confirmed detection of an exoplanet was in 1992 around a pulsar, and the first detection around a main-sequence star was in 1995.
This West Point graduate, eighth in his class of 670, commanded Apollo 8's historic flight around the Moon in 1968 — who is he?
Frank Borman (March 14, 1928 - November 7, 2023) was an American United States Air Force (USAF) colonel, aeronautical engineer, NASA astronaut, test pilot, and businessman.
Built from glutamate, cysteine and glycine, this tripeptide is the most abundant low-molecular-mass thiol in most cells and a key antioxidant guarding against free radicals — what is it?
Glutathione (GSH) is a tripeptide made of the amino acids glutamate, cysteine, and glycine.

In 1896 this English physician dosed himself with mescaline and wrote one of the first public reports of the trip; he also co-wrote English's first medical textbook on homosexuality and coined the term 'narcissism' — who was he?
Havelock Ellis (2 February 1859 - 8 July 1939) was an English physician, eugenicist, writer, progressive intellectual and social reformer who studied human sexuality.
Found from Alaska to Tierra del Fuego across roughly 375 species, the males of this American bird family boast the most diverse plumage colors of any birds — what are they?
Hummingbird are birds native to the Americas and comprise the biological family Trochilidae.
An ISO standard defines it as "a new or changed entity, realizing or redistributing value" — and it's related to, but not the same as, invention. What word are we after?
Innovation is the practical implementation of ideas that result in the creation or improvements of goods or services.
This psychologist edited 'Psychological Review' from 1910 to 1915 and was later ranked the 17th most-cited psychologist of the 20th century for popularizing behaviorism — who is he?
John B. Watson (January 9, 1878 - September 25, 1958) was an American psychologist who popularized the scientific theory of behaviorism, establishing it as a psychological school.
This unit of speed equals exactly one nautical mile per hour, roughly 1.15 mph, and is the standard measure used in maritime and aviation contexts — what is it called?
Knot (unit) is a unit of speed equal to one nautical mile per hour, exactly 1.852 km/h (approximately 1.151 mph or 0.514 m/s).
Also called the great grey slug, this 10-20cm mollusc has a strange courtship where mating pairs suspend themselves in midair from a mucus thread — what species is it?
Limax maximus (literally, "biggest slug"), known by the common names great grey slug and leopard slug, is a species of slug in the family Limacidae, the keeled slugs.

Resembling some toxic look-alikes despite being a well-regarded edible, this basidiomycete fungus is a fairly common species on well-drained soils across temperate Eurasia, found solitary or in fairy rings in pastures — name the species?
Macrolepiota procera is a basidiomycete fungus with a large, prominent fruiting body resembling a parasol.
First synthesized in 1982 near Darmstadt, this fleeting synthetic element of the periodic table's seventh period was named in 1997 after a pioneering Austrian-Swedish nuclear physicist. What is it?
Meitnerium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mt and atomic number 109.
This small, subterranean mammal has velvety fur, tiny eyes, and short powerful forelimbs with oversized paws built for constant digging — what animal is it?
In this category of over 80 recognized conditions, the body's adaptive immune system mistakenly attacks its own healthy tissue as though it were foreign. What is it?

Navel (clinically known as the umbilicus; pl.: umbilici or umbilicuses; also known as the belly button or tummy button) is a protruding, flat, or hollowed area on the abdomen at the attachment site of the umbilical cord.
This insect order includes dragonflies and damselflies, the bulkier ones holding wings out at rest while the slender ones fold theirs along the body — what is it?
Odonata is an order of predatory flying insects that includes the dragonflies and damselflies (as well as the Epiophlebia damsel-dragonflies).
Usually numbering four and tucked behind the thyroid, these small endocrine structures release a hormone that kicks in when blood calcium runs low — which structures?
Parathyroid gland are small endocrine glands in the neck of humans and other tetrapods.
What dissociative anesthetic, known on the street as a recreational drug, can cause hallucinations, paranoia, and psychotic behavior, and is often smoked or mixed with cannabis or tobacco?
Phencyclidine (PCP), also known in its use as a street drug as angel dust among other names, is a dissociative anesthetic mainly used recreationally for its significant mind-altering effects.
Named after the American diplomat who introduced it to the US in the 1820s, this red-and-green plant native to Mexico is a Christmas staple — what plant is it?
Poinsettia (Euphorbia pulcherrima) is a commercially important flowering plant species of the diverse spurge family Euphorbiaceae.
Split into roughly a dozen Afrotropical species and around 167 Neotropical species — among them the blue-and-yellow macaw and the grey parrot — which bird family is this?
Psittacidae is one of three families of true parrots.
What dimensionless quantity in fluid dynamics, expressing the ratio of inertial to viscous forces, determines whether a flow will be smooth and laminar or chaotic and turbulent?
Reynolds number (Re) is a dimensionless quantity that helps predict fluid flow patterns in different situations by measuring the ratio between inertial and viscous forces.
Named after an American veterinary surgeon, this genus of rod-shaped, gram-negative bacteria includes over 2,650 serotypes within a single major species — name it?
Salmonella is a genus of rod-shaped, (bacillus) Gram-negative bacteria of the family Enterobacteriaceae.

This dog breed from southern China, traditionally kept as a property guardian, was driven to the brink of extinction in the 20th century and is known in the West for its deep wrinkles. What breed is this?

Shar Pei (Cantonese; pinyin: sh p) is a dog breed from
southern China.
This birth defect involves incomplete closure of the spinal column and its surrounding membranes during early pregnancy, occurring in three recognized forms — what condition is it?
Spina bifida (SB; Latin for 'split spine') is a birth defect in which there is incomplete closing of the spine and the membranes around the spinal cord during early development in pregnancy.
Named for its long, flat, sword-like bill, this large migratory predatory fish loses all its teeth and scales by adulthood and is a popular target among billfish anglers — what is it?
Swordfish (Xiphias gladius), also known as the broadbill in some countries, are large, highly migratory predatory fish characterized by a long, flat, sword-like, pointed bill.

This weakly radioactive silvery metal, atomic number 90, tarnishes olive-grey in air, and its most stable isotope has a half-life of about 14 billion years — roughly the age of the universe. What element is this?
Thorium is a chemical element; it has symbol Th and atomic number 90.
An important food fish found in marine and brackish waters from the Baltic to the Mediterranean, this flatfish's Black Sea relatives are now classified as a separate species — which fish?
Turbot is a relatively large species of flatfish in the family Scophthalmidae.
What's the name for the small, non-cancerous skin growths caused by the human papillomavirus, most common on the hands and feet but also appearing as genital or filiform forms?
Wart are non-cancerous viral growths usually occurring on the hands and feet but which can also affect other locations, such as the genitals or face.

This paraphilia describes a sexual fixation on non-human animals, distinct from acting on such attraction, and was estimated in one 2021 study to affect about 2 percent of the population — name the term?
Zoophilia is a paraphilia in which a person experiences a sexual fixation on non-human animals.
Regarded as one of Formula One's greatest engineers, his car designs have won 14 Drivers' and 12 Constructors' Championships across three decades?
Adrian Newey: British engineer, aerodynamicist and motorsport executive (born 1958)
This Swedish chemist held 355 patents, invented dynamite, and then left his fortune to fund a famous set of prizes. Who was he?
Alfred Nobel: Swedish chemist and inventor (1833–1896)

Inspired by Ørsted's 1820 discovery that current creates a magnetic field, this principle relating a magnetic field's circulation to the current passing through a loop was later generalized by Maxwell with a displacement current term — which physics principle?
Ampère's circuital law: Concept in classical electromagnetism.

A political economy professor turned finance minister after a 1926 coup, this Portuguese dictator ruled his corporatist 'New State' from 1932 until 1968, in one of modern Europe's longest authoritarian regimes — who is he?
António de Oliveira Salazar: Prime Minister of Portugal from 1932 to 1968.

Also known by a folksy nickname, this small North American tree produces a custard-textured fruit tasting like banana or pineapple — despite containing a neurotoxin elsewhere in the plant. What species is it?
Asimina triloba: Species of tree. Asimina triloba, the American papaw, pawpaw, paw paw, or paw-paw, among many regional names, is a species of small deciduous tree.
As the largest member of the grass family, one species of this plant can grow stalks over 46 meters tall and 36 centimeters thick — name the plant?
Bamboo: Subfamily of plants in the grass family.

With arms and tentacles up to 26 feet long held at right angles to its body, this deep-sea cephalopod has been spotted as deep as 6,212 meters — the only one of its kind known to survive the hadal zone. What is it?

Developed in the 1980s-90s to replace an aging Cold War transport aircraft, this large military cargo plane carries forward the name of two earlier piston-engined predecessors, the C-74 and C-124. What is this modern behemoth called?
Boeing C-17 Globemaster III: American four engine military transport aircraft.

Affecting roughly 22% of people worldwide, this oral parafunctional habit — often during sleep and without the person's awareness — can leave you with aching jaw muscles, headaches, and worn-down teeth. What is it?
Bruxism: Grinding or clenching of the teeth.
When this yeast infection strikes the mouth it's commonly called thrush, leaving telltale white patches on the tongue — what is the condition?
Candidiasis: Fungal infection due to any type of Candida.
Responsible for nearly 40 percent of blindness cases worldwide in 2020, this condition clouds the eye's lens and causes halos around lights — which condition?
Cataract: Clouding of the lens inside the eye, causing poor vision.
Known as lamb's quarters, goosefoot, or fat-hen, this fast-growing annual weed in the amaranth family is sometimes cultivated as food elsewhere — which plant?
Chenopodium album: Species of flowering plant in the goosefoot family.
Native to the Indonesian island that gave part of its scientific name, this legume flower also goes by butterfly pea or blue pea — what is it?
Its species name honors Colchis, an ancient region on the Black Sea, and it's often released into the wild as a game bird — which Asian-native, ring-necked bird is this?
Common pheasant: Species of bird. The common pheasant (Phasianus colchicus), ring-necked pheasant, or blue-headed pheasant, is a bird in the pheasant family (Phasianidae).
First described in 1963, this rare disorder from a partial deletion on chromosome 5 gets its French name from the distinctive feline-sounding cry of affected infants — what is it called?
Cri du chat syndrome: Human medical condition.

This English broadcaster is the only person to have won BAFTA Awards in black-and-white, colour, high-definition, 3D, and 4K — a span made possible by a presenting career that began with Zoo Quest in 1954. Who is this natural historian?
David Attenborough: English broadcaster and natural historian (born 1926)

A lean, wedge-skulled medium canine found in Australia and split off from the New Guinea singing dog, this animal's very classification — dog, wolf, or its own species — is still hotly debated — what is it?
Dingo: Canid species native to Australia.

Anatomically like us, some of the oldest remains of this species come from Ethiopia's Omo-Kibish site, dated to roughly 233,000 to 196,000 years ago — what term distinguishes them from archaic humans?
Early modern human: Old Stone Age ''Homo sapiens''
This inner lining of the uterus sheds during menstruation but thickens dramatically to help form the placenta during pregnancy — what is it?
Endometrium: Lining of the mammalian uterus. It has a basal layer and a functional layer: the basal layer contains stem cells which regenerate the functional layer.
This warbler's head marking gives it its name — dark in the male, chestnut in the female — and its closest relative is the garden warbler. What bird is it?
Eurasian blackcap: Bird in the Old World warbler family from Eurasia and Africa.

Colloquially called squirting or gushing, this fluid is expelled from the Skene's gland near the urethra around the time of orgasm — and researchers stress it's physiologically distinct from coital incontinence. What is it?
Female ejaculation: Expulsion of fluid during orgasm.
A pungent colorless gas churned out at 26 million tons a year, it's used to make resins and, in a roughly 37% solution, to preserve tissue samples in labs — what is it?
Running from mouth to anus, this passageway includes the esophagus, stomach, and intestines and handles digestion and nutrient absorption — what is it?
Gastrointestinal tract: Organ system within humans and other animals.
As the single largest muscle in the human body, this hip extensor gives the buttocks their shape and is a key reason humans can stand upright, unlike other primates — what is it?
Gluteus maximus: Largest and most superficial of the three gluteal muscles.

Beginning as weakness in the feet and hands before spreading upward, this rapid-onset autoimmune condition attacks the peripheral nervous system and can require a ventilator in about 15% of cases — which disorder is this?
Guillain–Barré syndrome: Autoimmune disease. Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS) is a rapid-onset muscle weakness caused by the immune system damaging the peripheral nervous system.
Tapeworms, flukes and roundworms all fall under this broad name for any infection where parasitic worms take up residence in the body. What is the condition called?
Helminthiasis: Any macroparasitic disease caused by helminths.
Arching shrubs or twining vines in the genus Lonicera, some 158 species of this fragrant plant attract hummingbirds in North America — what is it?

Defined as a blood sodium level below 135 millimoles per liter, this condition can arise from drinking excessive water — or even too much beer — and in severe cases causes seizures or coma — what is it?
Hyponatremia: Low sodium concentration in the blood.

A former Communist Party official who was later sidelined by Nicolae Ceaușescu, this engineer-turned-politician emerged from Romania's 1989 revolution to become the country's first freely elected president — who is he?
Built from an umbrella-shaped bell of mesoglea that pulses to swim, this Cnidarian trails stinging tentacles and is the medusa phase of its complex life cycle — what is it?
Developed by a South Korean aerospace firm with Lockheed Martin and first flown in 2002, this supersonic jet trainer became the country's first indigenous supersonic aircraft — which aircraft family?
KAI T-50 Golden Eagle: Family of South Korean jet aircraft. It is South Korea's first indigenous supersonic aircraft and one of the world's few supersonic trainers.
This plant family — home to basil, rosemary, thyme, lavender, and sage — also counts teak among its rare tree species and chia among its edible seed crops — which family?
Also called May bells or Our Lady's tears, this woodland plant's sweetly scented white bell-flowers hide a dangerously poisonous secret — which flower?
Lily of the valley: Species of flowering plant in the asparagus family.
This best-known stag beetle species in Western Europe lends its genus its very name, and is currently listed as Near Threatened — what is it?
Lucanus cervus: Species of beetle. L. cervus is listed as Near Threatened by the IUCN Red List.
Sharing joints only with the temporal bones, this is the skull's lone movable bone, hosting the lower teeth and shrinking in size since humans began farming around 10,000 BCE — what is it called?
Mandible: Lower jaw bone. The mandible hosts the lower teeth (their depth delineated by the alveolar process).
Also known as flying foxes, these 197-plus species of fruit-eating bat likely evolved in Australasia some 31 million years ago — what are they called?

This medical condition, usually diagnosed shortly after birth, is defined as a length at least 2.5 standard deviations below the average and affects about 1.5 in 10,000 male newborns in North America. What is this condition?
First prepared in 1908 by biochemist Kikunae Ikeda as he tried to bottle the savory taste of kombu seaweed, this flavor enhancer is the original source of umami in cooking — what is it?
Monosodium glutamate: Flavor enhancer (621 or E621)
Native to southern Europe and North Africa, this fragrant evergreen shrub has berries that are macerated in alcohol to make Mirto liqueur — which plant?
Myrtus communis: Species of flowering plant.
This synthetic element 113 was claimed by both a Russian-American team at Dubna and, in 2004, a Japanese team at Riken. What's its name?
Nihonium: Chemical element with atomic number 113 (Nh)

Distinct from an unrelated American family with a similar name, these small seed-eating birds include house- and tree-dwelling species that nest on buildings in huge city numbers — which bird family is this?
Old World sparrow: Family of songbirds. Old World sparrows are groups of small passerine birds forming the family Passeridae.
Created by Rasmus Lerdorf in 1993, this scripting language's name began as 'Personal Home Page' before becoming a recursive backronym meaning 'Hypertext Preprocessor' — what is it?
PHP: Scripting language created in 1994. PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared towards web development.
Often described simply as the act of teaching, this discipline studies how knowledge and skills are imparted — and how that process shapes learners socially and psychologically. What is it?
Pedagogy: Theory and practice of education.
This toxic gas, which smells like freshly cut hay, was responsible for tens of thousands of deaths as a chemical weapon in World War I — what is it?
Named after the American diplomat who introduced it from Mexico, this red-and-green Christmas plant is not actually toxic to pets — which plant?
Also known as face blindness, this cognitive disorder leaves a person unable to recognize familiar faces — even their own — while other visual skills stay intact. What is it?
Prosopagnosia: Cognitive disorder of face perception. Prosopagnosia should not be confused with prosopometamorphopsia, a disorder characterized by altered perceptions of faces.
Some specimens of this native European tree, whose acorns dangle on long stalks, are believed to be over 1,000 years old — name the species?
Quercus robur: Species of flowering plant.
Striking children recovering from a viral illness like the flu, this brain disease has been linked in about 90% of cases to aspirin use — what is it called?
Reye syndrome: Rapidly worsening brain disease.
Discovered in 1861 via flame spectroscopy by Bunsen and Kirchhoff, this alkali metal is named from the Latin word for 'deep red' — which element?
Rubidium: Chemical element with atomic number 37 (Rb)

Though crustaceans within this food category are more closely related to insects and spiders than to true fish, what group — including molluscs, crustaceans, and echinoderms — ranks among the most common food allergens?
Shellfish: Culinary and fisheries term for exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates.
Once called 'hyposulphite of soda,' this reducing agent treats cyanide poisoning and served as photography's key fixer in the 19th century — what compound?
Sodium thiosulfate: Chemical compound. Sodium thiosulfate (sodium thiosulphate) is an inorganic compound with the formula Na2S2O3·xH2O.

An English dyer and astronomer, he was the first to systematically show, around 1729, that electricity could travel through metals — flipping the era's focus from mere static sparks to conduction. Who was he?
Stephen Gray (scientist): English physicist. Stephen Gray (December 1666 – February 1736) was an English dyer and astronomer who was the first to systematically experiment with electrical conduction.
Commonly known as fainting, this fast-onset, short-duration loss of consciousness and muscle strength is typically caused by a sudden drop in blood flow to the brain — what's the medical term?
Syncope (medicine): Transient loss of consciousness and postural tone.
Also sold under the name dronabinol, this principal psychoactive compound in cannabis is prescribed to relieve chemotherapy-induced nausea and HIV/AIDS-related appetite loss — what is it?
Tetrahydrocannabinol: Psychoactive component of cannabis. It is the principal psychoactive constituent of Cannabis and one of at least 113 total cannabinoids identified on the plant.
Sitting between cells and organs in the body's organization, this assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix takes its English name from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
Tissue (biology): Group of similar cells performing a specific function.
Roughly three times stiffer than steel and nearly as hard as diamond, this gray powder is sintered into cutting tools, armor-piercing bullets, and jewelry — what compound is it?
Tungsten carbide: Hard, dense and stiff chemical compound.
The brightest star in the constellation Lyra, this star sits just 25 light-years away and served as Earth's northern pole star around 12,000 BCE — which star?
Vega: Brightest star in the constellation Lyra. It has the Bayer designation α Lyrae, which is Latinised to Alpha Lyrae and abbreviated Alpha Lyr or α Lyr.
With a distinctive pale eye and grey nape against black plumage, this small, gregarious member of the crow family was first formally described by Linnaeus — name the bird?
Western jackdaw: Species of bird in the crow family Corvidae.
Also called the pikeperch, this ray-finned game fish native to western Eurasian waters is the type species that gave its whole genus a name — which fish?
Zander: Species of fish. The zander (Sander lucioperca), sander or pikeperch, is a species of ray-finned fish from the family Percidae (which also includes perch, ruffe and darter).
What is the chemical symbol for sulfur?
The symbol for sulfur is S. Sulfur, also spelled as sulphur, is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
